text: Here's an idea worth real money if it's right. Small satellite operators can't easily find spare capacity on rockets that are already flying. So build the marketplace, take a cut. Everyone you pitch it to will say it sounds great. None of them will have looked.

Clustral builds investigative agents. Things that go and look, then come back holding proof. This is Ignition, and it points that at the most expensive decision a founder ever makes. Committing a year to the wrong idea.
So. One sentence. A booking platform for smallsat operators, to compare and reserve rideshare slots across SpaceX, Rocket Lab and Isar Aerospace.

I'm replaying a recorded run, so the numbers hold still while I talk. All of it is real output. And watch what it does first. It writes its own research plan, without saying a word about the market. It can't. It hasn't looked.
There. Six searches at once. Who is already doing this. What the market is worth. And where operators are complaining.
Fifty four. Refine. And notice what it didn't say. It didn't say great idea. It picked a side, and it put a number on it.

My next question is, fifty four according to what? Sixteen points from Build. No single score gets there on its own. The most room left is in demand. And the verdict holds unless demand drops thirty one points. That stops being a score and starts being a brief.
Underneath it, twenty one exhibits. Numbered, like a case file. Every one of them a link I can open. Let me pull up just what the operators said.

And here's the finding I'd want. SpaceX already runs its own smallsat rideshare programme. SEOPS already sells the booking. Both carry the exhibit they came from. That's the honest answer to, is anyone doing this. And it isn't the one I wanted.

Then it hands me the week. Seven days, drawn entirely from this file. The competitor to go and use. The thread to go and read. And what to build first, which is an aggregated slot catalogue and nothing else.

This is what won me over. It marks its own homework. Every claim is sourced, but it leaned on only six of its twenty one exhibits, and lists three things it couldn't establish. It even flags that I gave it no domain key, so the names it suggests are labelled unverified.

Now watch. Same idea, cross examined. Questioned the way an investor would before writing a cheque. And it went up. Sixty five. Looking for reasons this fails, it found a growing market, not a saturated one. A tool that only confirms your fears is as useless as one that only confirms your hopes.
Command K takes me anywhere in the file. And the whole thing exports as one document. Verdict, exhibits, the week. Something I can hand to a co-founder.
Live evidence. A verdict that commits. And a week of work waiting on the other side. Ignition, from Clustral. Don't build it, until you validate it.
